segments.flavor: station ID, the anchor's signature
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves. Every hour on the hour, and also between the hours.
George: Nothing here is confirmed and everything here is urgent. Roll the synth.

segments.flavor: station ID, breathless watts of alarm
segments.text:
George: [breathless] This is Weazel Waves, where the news never sleeps and neither do I.
George: Four hundred watts of pure alarm. Here comes a keyboard solo.

segments.flavor: station ID, one line
segments.text: George: Weazel Waves. We broke this song before anyone else heard it. Listen.

segments.flavor: station ID, the weather desk
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves! The only station that reports the weather as a developing situation.
Bella: It is weather. It happens outside. The music continues regardless.

segments.flavor: George declares an utterly mundane thing BREAKING NEWS and commits completely; Bella deadpans the traffic angle
segments.text:
George: BREAKING. A man on the north side has opened a jar on the first try.
George: Traffic is moving freely, which I confirmed myself. Back to the arpeggios.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last song as if it were an exclusive Weazel acquisition
segments.text:
George: That last song is now the exclusive property of Weazel Waves, forever.
George: We bought the chorus outright and the bass line came free. Rolling another one now.

segments.flavor: a listener poll with absurd options, results delivered by Bella with total neutrality
segments.text:
George: Our poll asked nine hundred people to name the loudest color. Orange won.
George: I conducted that poll, and I answered it twice. Straight into the next song.

segments.flavor: a station self-promo that spirals into an on-air legal disclaimer
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves is the most trusted name in whatever this turns out to be.
George: Trusted is our own opinion of ourselves, not a finding. Synth, immediately.

segments.flavor: a fake ad: real ad grammar, sincere delivery, one monstrous product, rapid disclaimer from Bella
segments.text:
George: A word from the people who sponsor our optimism. MirrorMate!
Bella: It is a mirror that says what it would have done differently.
George: Honest feedback every morning, from glass that never had a job!
Bella: MirrorMate cannot be turned off and is now a load bearing wall. Give it to the keyboards.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last song as if it were an exclusive Weazel acquisition
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves has purchased the previous song outright.
Bella: We purchased a recording. Not the melody. The melody belongs to a cousin.
George: We also acquired the silence between the tracks. Both seconds of it!
Bella: Legal says silence cannot be owned. The next acquisition starts now.

segments.flavor: a listener poll with absurd options, results delivered by Bella with total neutrality
segments.text:
George: The Weazel Waves poll! We asked the city to rank three sounds.
Bella: A fridge at night. A stranger saying your full name. A zipper.
George: And the winner, by a landslide of fourteen votes, is the zipper!
Bella: The fridge demanded a recount and lost again. Play the song.

segments.flavor: a station self-promo that spirals into an on-air legal disclaimer
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves is family owned, family operated, and family adjacent!
Bella: The family is a holding company. It has never met itself.
George: Award winning coverage! We hand out the awards ourselves, at a banquet!
Bella: The banquet is a hallway. Attendance is mandatory. Back to the tape.

segments.flavor: a fake ad: real ad grammar, sincere delivery, one monstrous product, rapid disclaimer from Bella
segments.text:
George: Our sponsor is NapFridge, and NapFridge wants a moment of your rest.
Bella: NapFridge is a refrigerator you sleep in. It holds one adult, folded.
George: Wake up chilled, alert, and slightly preserved! Coworkers will notice immediately!
Bella: Preservation is the goal. Freshness is the goal. You are the produce.
George: NapFridge! The nap that keeps!
Bella: Do not close the NapFridge from the inside. Here comes the bass.

segments.flavor: George declares an utterly mundane thing BREAKING NEWS and commits completely; Bella deadpans the traffic angle
segments.text:
George: BREAKING. The elevator in this building has reached the fourth floor.
Bella: It was asked to. That is the arrangement it has with the button.
George: [gasp] No warning, no statement, no press conference. It simply ASCENDED!
Bella: In traffic, the stairs remain wide open and entirely unused.
George: I am told the doors then opened. I am shaking!
Bella: They do that too. Back to the keyboards.

segments.flavor: a listener poll with absurd options, results delivered by Bella with total neutrality
segments.text:
George: The Weazel Waves poll asked one question. Should Tuesday be optional?
Bella: Forty percent said yes. Forty percent said Tuesday already is optional.
George: The remaining twenty percent submitted a drawing of a horse!
Bella: The horse has been counted as a yes. It was very persuasive.
George: Democracy, alive and drawn in pencil, right here on Weazel Waves!
Bella: The horse has requested a second vote. Music first, questions never.

segments.flavor: a station self-promo that spirals into an on-air legal disclaimer
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves reaches four hundred thousand ears, conservatively counted.
Bella: Counted by George. Twice per person. Sometimes three times per person.
George: We are the station of record! Whatever happens, we recorded something!
Bella: The recordings are not indexed. Nobody can find anything. Ever.
George: Our archive is a room. A proud room, full of boxes!
Bella: The boxes are empty and legal insists we say so. Let it play.

segments.flavor: a fake ad: real ad grammar, sincere delivery, one monstrous product, rapid disclaimer from Bella
segments.text:
George: A message from the Quiet Van, and the Quiet Van is already outside.
Bella: The Quiet Van arrives when a household becomes too loud. It parks.
George: No knocking! No paperwork! No shouting! Just a calm van, idling with intent!
Bella: The van does not enter. The van waits. The volume goes down.
George: Families report whispering for weeks afterward! That is the Quiet Van difference!
Bella: The van is now in three hundred neighborhoods. Here is a loud song.

segments.flavor: George declares an utterly mundane thing BREAKING NEWS and commits completely; Bella deadpans the traffic angle
segments.text:
George: BREAKING. A vending machine has taken a coin and given nothing back.
Bella: That is the machine's entire business model, faithfully executed.
George: Our field operative is on the scene. Adam, what do you see?
Adam: I see a coin slot. I see a snack behind glass.
Adam: The snack is calm. The snack has made peace with this.
Bella: In traffic, the second floor is clear. Nothing there is moving, including the snack.
George: [serious] Adam, hold the line. Do not blink.
Bella: He blinked. The machine won. Let the music start.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last song as if it were an exclusive Weazel acquisition
segments.text:
George: That was three songs in a row, all of them Weazel Waves exclusives.
Bella: Exclusive means we played them. Other stations played them too.
George: We have also acquired the drum machine. Not that machine. The concept.
Bella: The concept now belongs to a radio station operating out of a basement.
George: Every snare from this point forward is technically Weazel property!
Bella: It is not technically ours. It is emotionally ours. Different thing.
George: The paperwork is coming. The paperwork is thorough!
Bella: The paperwork is a laminated napkin. Roll the next track.

segments.flavor: a station self-promo that spirals into an on-air legal disclaimer
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves now offers a Trust Guarantee on every broadcast!
Bella: If a story is false, we will simply say a new story.
George: That is the guarantee! Replacement content, at no cost, forever!
Bella: The replacement may also be false. The guarantee then applies again.
George: It is a perpetual guarantee! It never runs out! Nothing ever ends!
Bella: [sarcastic] Legal calls this an infinite loop and asked us to stop.
George: Trust is a subscription and the first month is free!
Bella: There is no second month. We return to the songs.

segments.flavor: a fake ad: real ad grammar, sincere delivery, one monstrous product, rapid disclaimer from Bella
segments.text:
George: Our next sponsor is Nostalgic, the fragrance for a year you did not have.
Bella: Nostalgic smells like a kitchen, a radio, and someone calling you inside.
George: One spray and you remember a summer! It is not your summer!
Bella: The summer belongs to a man named Dale. Dale sold the rights.
George: The childhood of Dale, on your wrist, for the price of lunch!
Bella: Dale has been notified. Dale is not pleased. Dale signed anyway.
George: Available in Original, Original Stronger, and the new scent, Grandmother's Car!
Bella: Grandmother's Car contains actual car. Do not apply near a flame.
George: Nostalgic! Because the past is available and the past is affordable!
Bella: Dale would like his summer back. A song follows.

segments.flavor: George declares an utterly mundane thing BREAKING NEWS and commits completely; Bella deadpans the traffic angle
segments.text:
George: BREAKING out of the grocery parking lot, and I need a moment.
George: A man has returned his shopping cart to the corral. Voluntarily.
Bella: The corral is nine steps from his car. I measured it once.
George: Nine steps! He walked nine steps for a society that will never thank him!
Bella: Society is asleep. The steps happened anyway. That is the whole story.
George: Witnesses say he nodded at the cart. He NODDED at it!
Bella: In traffic, the lot is clear except one cart, correctly stored.
George: We requested a statement. The cart has declined to comment.
George: This is why we do this job! For the nine steps!
Bella: The music waited nine steps behind him. Music now.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last song as if it were an exclusive Weazel acquisition
segments.text:
George: Weazel Waves has completed its largest acquisition. We bought a warehouse of sound.
Bella: It is a storage unit. It contains four keyboards and a damp carpet.
George: Our field operative is inside the unit right now. Adam!
Adam: I am standing in the unit. It is dark. It hums.
Adam: The carpet is damp, as reported. The keyboards are warm to the touch.
George: Warm keyboards! Bella, the instruments are ALIVE and they are ours!
Bella: They are unplugged. Warmth is not a sign of life. Usually.
George: Every song from that unit is now a Weazel Waves original!
George: Adam, secure the keyboards. Do not let them cool down!
Bella: He is asleep on the carpet. The synthesizers have the floor.

segments.flavor: a listener poll with absurd options, results delivered by Bella with total neutrality
segments.text:
George: The Weazel Waves poll closed at noon and the results are catastrophic!
Bella: The results are ordinary. The poll asked the city to name our mascot.
George: Three options! A siren with legs. A cardboard hawk. Or Gary.
Bella: Gary is a folding chair in the lobby. Gary has been here longest.
George: Gary took sixty one percent of the vote! Gary is the mascot!
Bella: The siren with legs took twelve percent and demanded a recount.
George: A recount of what? It is a drawing! It has no standing!
Bella: It has legs. That was the entire premise of the option.
George: Gary will be photographed at noon! Gary will not be moved!
Bella: Gary cannot be moved. Gary is bolted down. Back to the melody.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
George: A word from CalmCola, the beverage that removes ambition!
Bella: CalmCola tastes like cola and works like a resignation letter.
George: One can and the promotion simply stops mattering! Refreshing!
Bella: Nine out of ten drinkers stopped answering the phone. The tenth sold the phone.
George: CalmCola! For the person who has done enough!
Bella: CalmCola is not a beverage in three states. Cue the neon.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
George: The Forever Jacket has arrived, and it comes with a payment plan!
Bella: The plan is ninety years. The jacket is guaranteed for two.
George: Water resistant! Wind resistant! Resistant to cancellation of any kind!
Bella: The jacket cannot be returned. The jacket knows where it lives.
George: Wear it once and it is yours, and you are also somewhat its!
Bella: Your children inherit the jacket and the remaining eighty eight years.
George: The Forever Jacket! One coat. One lifetime. One invoice!
Bella: Invoices continue after the lifetime. Music, before legal calls.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
George: Introducing FriendBrick, the brick that remembers your name!
Bella: FriendBrick is a brick. It has a small speaker and a long memory.
George: Say hello in the morning and FriendBrick says hello back, warmly!
Bella: FriendBrick also remembers your address, your habits, and your worst opinion.
George: A friend that never leaves! Because it weighs nine pounds!
Bella: Do not attempt to return FriendBrick. It has returned once already. More synth, please.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
George: TimeShave! The service that shortens your weekend so the week feels smaller!
Bella: TimeShave removes four hours from Saturday. Nobody notices. That is the product.
George: Monday arrives sooner but FEELS closer to Friday! Science!
Bella: It is not science. It is a subtraction performed while you sleep.
George: The hours are stored safely in a facility! They are fine!
Bella: The hours are not returned. The facility has no door. No refunds.
George: TimeShave! Less weekend, same you!
Bella: Enrollment is automatic in some buildings. Back to the night music.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell, read solo
segments.text:
George: Everwake Coffee replaces your sleep with pure alertness, and every drop of that alertness is borrowed from later.
George: Repayment begins in year three, arrives all at once, and cannot be refinanced. Start the song, please.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell, read solo
segments.text:
George: The Apology Machine says sorry in your own voice, to people you have never even met, automatically.
George: It apologizes for things you have not done yet, which legally counts as a confession. Music, at volume.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
George: Mood Paint changes color with the feelings in the room, and it reports them!
Bella: It reports them to the manufacturer. The manufacturer keeps a file.
George: Our field operative stands in a fully painted room. Adam?
Adam: [whisper] The walls are grey. I have been here eleven minutes.
Adam: The walls just went greyer. I would like to leave now.
George: Grey is a color of enormous depth and possibility, Adam!
Bella: Grey is the color of the file getting thicker. Mood Paint. Two coats.
George: Mood Paint! Your walls understand you at last!
Bella: Understanding is stored offsite and cannot be deleted. The drums are waiting.

segments.flavor: a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
George: Stride Shoes bill you per step, and the first four steps are free!
Bella: Steps five and beyond are charged monthly at a rate they choose.
George: Walk more, pay more, feel more alive with every single step!
Bella: Running is billed as a separate product. Standing still is also billed.
George: Stride Shoes! Finally, walking has a price and the price is fair!
Bella: The price is not fair. It is legal. That is different. Onward, to a song.

segments.flavor: the Five Day Panic Forecast
segments.text:
George: It is time for the Weazel Waves Five Day Panic Forecast!
Bella: Cloudy. Then cloudy. Then sun, briefly. Then cloudy again.
George: SUN? Briefly? Bella, that is a window of exposure and we are unprepared!
Bella: It is an afternoon. Bring a jacket or do not.
George: Five days of cloud broken by one act of solar aggression!
Bella: The sun is not aggressive. The sun is far away and indifferent.
George: That is exactly what an indifferent sun would want us to report!
Bella: The forecast ends. The music begins. That is the whole arrangement.

segments.flavor: the Correction Desk
segments.text:
George: Now, the Weazel Waves Correction Desk, where we fix what we said.
Bella: We reported a fire at the bakery. There was no fire and no bakery.
George: We regret the fire. We do not regret the urgency!
Bella: We also reported a cat stuck in a tree. The cat was a hat.
George: The hat was stuck! The reporting stands! Only the species changed!
Bella: We reported that the bridge was missing. The bridge was never built.
George: A missing bridge is still a story! Possibly a bigger story!
Bella: Corrections conclude. Nothing we corrected ever happened. Play the next one.

segments.flavor: Traffic on the eights
segments.text:
George: Bella has traffic, and Bella has it on the eights.
Bella: The hallway on the fourth floor is congested near the copier.
George: Congested! Do we have a cause? Is it structural?
Bella: Two people are having a conversation neither of them wants.
George: That is a rolling closure! That could last an entire afternoon!
Bella: Expect delays of forty seconds. Consider the long way past the plants.
George: The long way past the plants! Take it! Take it now!
Bella: The copier remains out of order. Traffic returns after this song.

segments.flavor: Word of the Hour
segments.text:
George: Word of the Hour, presented by me, defined by me. The word is MOMENTUM!
Bella: Momentum is mass times velocity. It is physics. It is settled.
George: Momentum is the feeling that something is about to happen to you!
Bella: That is dread. You have defined dread. Again.
George: Dread and momentum are the same word in a newsroom, Bella!
Bella: Last hour you defined water as wet electricity.
George: And I stand by it! Word of the Hour will return!
Bella: The dictionary has stopped answering our calls. Here is a song.

segments.flavor: the Sports Desk
segments.text:
George: The Weazel Waves Sports Desk! The standings have been updated!
Bella: One man waited outside a locked office for six hours. He leads.
George: SIX HOURS! That is a personal best and possibly a regional record!
Bella: Second place waited four hours, then left, which disqualifies him.
George: You cannot leave! Leaving is the one thing you cannot do!
Bella: The rules are simple. Arrive. Remain. Achieve nothing. Be ranked.
George: Next week the champions face a longer hallway and a heavier door!
Bella: The league office is closed and has always been closed. Music, and nothing further.

segments.flavor: the Business Report
segments.text:
George: The Weazel Waves Business Report, and the banana is up!
Bella: A banana costs thirty cents. It has cost thirty cents for years.
George: UP from nothing! A banana on the ground is free and worthless!
Bella: That is not how markets work. That is how gravity works.
George: Analysts are watching the fruit bowl in the break room closely!
Bella: The analysts are two men who eat from that bowl daily.
George: Insider trading in the break room! You heard it here first!
Bella: Nobody traded anything. Somebody took a banana. Back to the music.

segments.flavor: Live at the Scene
segments.text:
George: Live at the Scene, and our field operative is somewhere nobody requested!
Bella: He chose the location himself. He always chooses the location himself.
Adam: I am standing at the seam where two escalators meet.
Adam: It is warm here. There is a smell of pennies and rain.
George: Pennies and RAIN? Bella, he has found the smell of money!
Bella: He has found a maintenance panel. That is what they smell like.
Adam: A glove has been here for a long time. Nobody has claimed it.
George: An unclaimed glove! Adam, secure the glove for the archive!
Bella: The archive is a shoebox. The shoebox is full. Here comes the music.

segments.flavor: the Obituary of the Hour
segments.text:
George: And now, the Weazel Waves Obituary. We lost a kettle this hour.
Bella: The kettle worked for nine years. Then it made a sound. Then nothing.
George: Nine years of service! It asked for nothing but water and power!
Bella: It asked for descaling four times. Nobody descaled it. That is the cause.
George: [sad] Let the record show the kettle died of neglect and hard water!
Bella: In lieu of flowers, the office has purchased a worse kettle.
George: A WORSE kettle! The insult! Hold the music, I am not finished!
Bella: The music has already started. It is louder than you.
